skill.name: microsoft-teams-automation
skill.description: Automate Microsoft Teams messaging, chats, meetings, channels, membership, and message searches through the Rube MCP integration.
skill.summary: Run common Microsoft Teams workflows through current Rube MCP tool schemas.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The Markdown backticks and identifier examples are not executable commands or reconnaissance, so 59 static findings are false positives. The external Rube MCP endpoint is a real low-severity trust boundary, and write workflows lack explicit confirmation gates.

remediation.issue: Consequential Teams writes do not require a final user confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Preview the destination, recipients, meeting time, and proposed change, then require confirmation immediately before each write operation.

remediation.issue: The skill routes Teams operations through an external Rube MCP endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Document the third-party data path, request least-privileged Microsoft permissions, and require users to review the OAuth consent before connecting.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Microsoft Teams connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `microsoft_teams`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
1. `MICROSOFT_TEAMS_TEAMS_LIST` - List teams to find target team [Prerequisite]
- `end_date_time`: ISO 8601 end time (must be after start)
- `participants`: Array of user objects with user_id and role
2. `MICROSOFT_TEAMS_GET_TEAM` - Get details for a specific team [Optional]
7. `MICROSOFT_TEAMS_ADD_MEMBER_TO_TEAM` - Add a member to the team [Optional]
- `query`: KQL search query (supports from:, sent:, attachments, boolean logic)
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- team_id must be a valid UUID format
- channel_id must be in thread format (e.g., '19:abc@thread.tacv2')
- `participants`: Array of user objects with user_id and role
- Participants require valid Microsoft user_id (GUID) values, not emails
- GET_CHANNEL returns 404 if team_id or channel_id is wrong
| Add team member | MICROSOFT_TEAMS_ADD_MEMBER_TO_TEAM | team_id, user_id |
| Get chat message | MICROSOFT_TEAMS_GET_CHAT_MESSAGE | chat_id, message_id |
- 403 errors indicate insufficient permissions or team access

content.value_statement: Routine Teams work requires many manual lookups and repeated actions. This skill guides Claude or Codex through current Rube MCP tools for reliable execution.
actual_capabilities: Lists accessible teams and resolves channel identifiers before posting.
Sends messages to Teams channels, direct chats, and group chats.
Creates standalone online meetings with specified participants and times.
Lists, creates, and inspects channels within accessible teams.
Lists team members and adds a selected user to a team.
Searches Teams messages with KQL queries and handles paginated results.
limitations: Requires a configured Rube MCP server and an active Microsoft Teams connection.
Available actions depend on Microsoft Graph permissions and tenant policies.
Created online meetings are not calendar events unless an Outlook calendar tool is used.
Search results can be delayed, and Microsoft Graph can throttle frequent requests.

prompt_templates.title: List My Teams
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Rube MCP to list the Microsoft Teams I can access. Show names and identifiers, and do not make changes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Channel Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the team named [team] and channel named [channel]. Draft this update: [message]. Show the destination and draft before posting.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Teams Meeting
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve these participants: [people]. Prepare a Teams meeting titled [subject] from [start] to [end] in [timezone]. Confirm details before creation.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Update a Team
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [team], list its channels and members, then propose changes for [goal]. Execute only approved changes and report each result.

output_examples.input: List channels in the Product team.
Prepare a release notice for Engineering announcements.
output_examples.output: Destination: Engineering > Announcements. Draft: Release 4.2 begins at 18:00 UTC. Confirmation is required before posting.

output_examples.input: Create a meeting for the migration review.
output_examples.output: Prepared meeting: Migration Review, 14:00-14:45 UTC, with three resolved participants. Confirmation is required before creation.

best_practices: Search for current tool schemas before every workflow because MCP parameters can change.
Resolve teams, channels, users, and chats through list operations instead of guessing identifiers.
Preview destinations and content, then obtain explicit approval before write operations.
anti_patterns: Do not post messages, create meetings, or change membership from ambiguous instructions.
Do not reuse identifiers across tenants or assume display names are unique.
Do not retry throttled requests immediately; honor Retry-After and use bounded backoff.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Configure the Rube MCP endpoint, connect Microsoft Teams through OAuth, and confirm the connection is active.

faq.question: Does the skill need a Microsoft API key?
faq.answer: No direct API key is documented. Rube MCP uses a Microsoft OAuth connection that users must review and authorize.

faq.question: Can it send channel and chat messages?
faq.answer: Yes. It can resolve destinations and use the available Teams tools to send channel, direct, or group messages.

faq.question: Can it create calendar events?
faq.answer: The Teams meeting tool creates a standalone online meeting. A calendar-linked meeting requires an Outlook calendar tool.

faq.question: Why can message search miss recent posts?
faq.answer: Teams search is eventually consistent. New messages can take 30 to 60 seconds to appear.

faq.question: How are permission errors handled?
faq.answer: A 403 response indicates missing permissions or team access. Review OAuth scopes and tenant consent before retrying.
